newsitem.title: SPAIN: SWIMMING-EUROPEAN GOLD FOR IRELAND'S OLYMPIC CHAMPION.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-EUROPEAN GOLD FOR IRELAND'S OLYMPIC CHAMPION.

text.p: Ireland's triple Olympic champion Michelle de Bruin made a victorious start to her European championship campaign when she clinched the gold in the women's 400 metres individual medley on Tuesday.
But De Bruin, formerly Michelle Smith but now competing under her married name, had to withstand a fine challenge from 15-year-old European junior champion Yana Klochkova.
De Bruin opened a lead on the initial butterfly leg but the Ukrainian youngster hit back on the backstroke, taking the lead and holding it through the breaststroke and first length of the freestyle.
De Bruin, however, drew on her greater resources of strength in the last 50 metres of the race and won by nearly a second in four minutes 42.08 seconds.
Klochkova was second in 4:43.07 and Hana Cerna of the Czech Republic third in 4:44.05.
Olympic silver medallist Sandra Voelker swept to victory in the women's 100 metres freestyle to give Germany the first pool swimming title of the championships.
Voelker, fastest qualifier in the morning's heats, led at the turn in the 50-metre San Pablo pool and just held off a late challenge by Slovakia's Martina Moravcova.
Voelker won in 55.38, with Moravcova taking the silver in 55.46 and Germany's Antje Buschschulte the bronze in 55.50.
Alexander Goukov clinched gold for Belarus, edging 1988 Olympic silver medallist Karoly Guttler of Hungary into second place in the men's 100 breaststroke.
Goukov, the world short-course 200 breaststroke champion, came through powerfully on the return length and won by just 0.06 seconds from Guttler in 1:02.23
Daniel Malek of the Czech Republic was just 0.04 seconds back for the bronze. Olympic champion Frederik DeBurghgraeve of Belgium did not defend his title.
Britain's Paul Palmer, silvethe 1995 European championships in the 400 freestyle, went one better and won the gold in the men's 200 freestyle.
Palmer produced a superb finishing burst to overhaul Italy's Massimo Rosolino, fastest qualifier from the morning's heats .
Palmer won in 1:48.85, with Rosolino second in 1:49.02 and Bela Szabados of Hungary third in 1:49.98.
James Salter just missed a second medal in the race for Britain, touching a tantalising 0.01 seconds behind Szabados in fourth place.
